name: Energy
desc: Companies that find, pump, move, refine and sell oil, gas and coal, plus the contractors and equipment makers that serve them.
note: Renewable power generators are not here; they sit in Utilities. Solar panel makers are classified as Semiconductors in Information Technology.

name: Energy
desc: The whole sector is a single industry group. It splits in two: companies that supply equipment and services to producers, and companies that own the oil, gas and coal itself.

name: Energy Equipment & Services
desc: The "picks and shovels" of oil and gas: firms hired by producers to drill wells and keep them running. Their fortunes follow producers' budgets.

name: Oil & Gas Drilling
desc: Owners and operators of land and offshore drilling rigs, rented to producers on contract. Rig day-rates swing hard with the oil price.

name: Oil & Gas Equipment & Services
desc: Makers of oilfield equipment and providers of services such as seismic surveys, well completion, pressure pumping and maintenance.

name: Oil, Gas & Consumable Fuels
desc: Companies that own the hydrocarbons, from the well to the pump, plus coal and uranium producers.

name: Integrated Oil & Gas
desc: The majors: companies that explore, produce, refine and market at scale, often with chemicals operations too.

name: Oil & Gas Exploration & Production
desc: "Upstream" companies that find and extract oil and gas. Their earnings track commodity prices most directly.

name: Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing
desc: "Downstream" refiners that turn crude into gasoline, diesel and jet fuel and sell it. Profit depends on the spread between crude and product prices.

name: Oil & Gas Storage & Transportation
desc: "Midstream" pipelines, storage terminals, gathering and processing plants, and oil and gas tankers. Revenue is often fee-based.

name: Coal & Consumable Fuels
desc: Producers of thermal coal and of fuels such as uranium used for power generation.
note: Miners of metallurgical (coking) coal used in steelmaking are classified under Steel in Materials.

name: Materials
desc: Companies that make or extract the basic materials other industries build with: chemicals, cement, packaging, metals, paper.

name: Materials
desc: One industry group holding five industries, from chemical plants to gold mines.

name: Chemicals
desc: From high-volume petrochemicals to specialized formulas. The largest Materials industry by number of sub-industries.

name: Commodity Chemicals
desc: High-volume basic chemicals, plastics, synthetic fibers and films, sold mainly on price.

name: Diversified Chemicals
desc: Producers with broad portfolios that don't fit a single chemical category.

name: Fertilizers & Agricultural Chemicals
desc: Makers of nitrogen, phosphate and potash fertilizers, pesticides and other farm chemicals.

name: Industrial Gases
desc: Producers of oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen and other gases, often supplied through long contracts from on-site plants.

name: Specialty Chemicals
desc: Chemicals sold for what they do rather than by the ton: paints and coatings, adhesives, additives, flavors and fragrances.

name: Construction Materials
desc: Heavy, local businesses supplying the raw stuff of building. Transport costs keep competition regional.

name: Construction Materials
desc: Producers of cement, aggregates (sand, gravel, crushed stone), ready-mix concrete and bricks.

name: Containers & Packaging
desc: The containers and packaging that consumer and industrial goods ship in.

name: Metal, Glass & Plastic Containers
desc: Makers of cans, bottles, jars and rigid plastic containers.

name: Paper & Plastic Packaging Products & Materials
desc: Makers of corrugated boxes, cartons, paper bags and flexible plastic packaging.

name: Metals & Mining
desc: Miners and producers of metals and minerals, sorted by their main commodity.

name: Aluminum
desc: Producers of aluminum and aluminum products, including bauxite mining and alumina refining.

name: Diversified Metals & Mining
desc: Miners of several metals, or of minerals without their own sub-industry, such as lithium, nickel, zinc and rare earths.

name: Copper
desc: Miners and producers of copper.

name: Gold
desc: Gold miners and producers, including royalty and streaming companies focused on gold.

name: Precious Metals & Minerals
desc: Miners of platinum, palladium, diamonds and other precious metals and gems besides gold and silver.

name: Silver
desc: Primary silver miners and producers.

name: Steel
desc: Steel producers and mills, plus miners of metallurgical (coking) coal used to make steel.

name: Paper & Forest Products
desc: Companies that harvest timber and turn wood into lumber, pulp and paper.

name: Forest Products
desc: Timber, lumber and other wood products.
note: Timber companies structured as REITs are classified in Real Estate (Timber REITs).

name: Paper Products
desc: Makers of paper and pulp. Paper made into packaging belongs in Containers & Packaging.

name: Industrials
desc: Companies that build capital goods, provide services to businesses, and move people and freight.
drivers: The business cycle and capital spending
note: Since 2023, payroll and business-process outsourcing companies sit here (Data Processing & Outsourced Services), moved over from Information Technology.

name: Capital Goods
desc: Companies that make the equipment, structures and systems other businesses invest in. Seven industries, from jet engines to distributors.

name: Aerospace & Defense
desc: Civil and military aircraft, engines, weapons systems and defense electronics.

name: Aerospace & Defense
desc: Makers of aircraft and aircraft parts, defense equipment, and related technology and services.

name: Building Products
desc: The manufactured components that go into buildings.

name: Building Products
desc: Makers of HVAC systems, windows, doors, insulation, plumbing fixtures and similar components. Lumber and cement are in Materials.

name: Construction & Engineering
desc: Contractors and engineers who design and build.

name: Construction & Engineering
desc: Non-residential contractors and engineering firms that build infrastructure, plants and commercial projects.
note: Homebuilders are in Consumer Discretionary (Homebuilding).

name: Electrical Equipment
desc: Equipment that generates, transmits and uses electricity.

name: Electrical Components & Equipment
desc: Wires and cables, switchgear, motors, batteries, lighting and similar electrical products.

name: Heavy Electrical Equipment
desc: Turbines, generators, large transformers and other power-generation equipment.

name: Industrial Conglomerates
desc: Diversified industrial groups.

name: Industrial Conglomerates
desc: Companies running several industrial businesses where no single one dominates enough to classify them elsewhere.

name: Machinery
desc: Machines that make, move and dig.

name: Construction Machinery & Heavy Transportation Equipment
desc: Earthmovers, mining equipment, heavy trucks, locomotives, rail cars and ships. Passenger cars are in Consumer Discretionary.

name: Agricultural & Farm Machinery
desc: Tractors, harvesters, irrigation and other farm equipment.

name: Industrial Machinery & Supplies & Components
desc: Factory machinery, pumps, valves, bearings, tools and the components that go into industrial equipment.

name: Trading Companies & Distributors
desc: Middlemen for industrial goods.

name: Trading Companies & Distributors
desc: Distributors of industrial equipment and supplies, plus trading houses such as Japan's sogo shosha.

name: Commercial & Professional Services
desc: Services sold to businesses and governments: facilities, waste, staffing, consulting, data processing.

name: Commercial Services & Supplies
desc: Operational services and supplies that keep organizations running.

name: Commercial Printing
desc: Printers of business forms, labels, documents and marketing materials.

name: Environmental & Facilities Services
desc: Waste collection and disposal, recycling, remediation and facilities management.

name: Office Services & Supplies
desc: Office supplies, office furniture and related services.

name: Diversified Support Services
desc: Outsourced business support such as uniform rental, equipment rental and auction services.

name: Security & Alarm Services
desc: Security guards, alarm monitoring and correctional facility operators.

name: Professional Services
desc: Expertise and labor sold by the hour, by the head or by the transaction.

name: Human Resource & Employment Services
desc: Staffing agencies, recruiters and HR outsourcing.

name: Research & Consulting Services
desc: Consultancies, research firms, credit bureaus, and testing and inspection companies.

name: Data Processing & Outsourced Services
desc: Payroll processors, business process outsourcing and back-office data services.
note: Moved into Industrials from Information Technology in the 2023 revision.

name: Transportation
desc: Companies that move people and freight, and those that own the infrastructure they move on.

name: Air Freight & Logistics
desc: Parcel delivery, air freight and logistics.

name: Air Freight & Logistics
desc: Parcel carriers, air freight operators and freight forwarders.

name: Passenger Airlines
desc: Airlines that carry people.

name: Passenger Airlines
desc: Passenger airlines, full-service and low-cost. Renamed from Airlines in 2023.

name: Marine Transportation
desc: Shipping of goods other than oil and gas.

name: Marine Transportation
desc: Container lines and dry-bulk carriers.
note: Oil and gas tankers are classified in Energy (Oil & Gas Storage & Transportation).

name: Ground Transportation
desc: Railroads, trucking and passenger road transport. Renamed from Road & Rail in 2023.

name: Rail Transportation
desc: Freight and passenger railroads.

name: Cargo Ground Transportation
desc: Trucking companies and truck and trailer leasing.

name: Passenger Ground Transportation
desc: Ride-hailing platforms, bus operators, taxis and car rental.

name: Transportation Infrastructure
desc: Owners and operators of the fixed assets that transport runs on.

name: Airport Services
desc: Airport operators and airport service companies.

name: Highways & Railtracks
desc: Toll roads, bridges, tunnels and rail track owners.

name: Marine Ports & Services
desc: Port operators and related marine services.

name: Consumer Discretionary
desc: Goods and services people want but can put off: cars, clothes, travel, dining out, most retail.
note: Amazon sits here (Broadline Retail), not in Information Technology. Since 2023, retailers that mainly sell staples, such as Walmart, Costco and Target, are in Consumer Staples.

name: Automobiles & Components
desc: Carmakers and the suppliers of parts that go into vehicles.

name: Automobile Components
desc: Parts suppliers to vehicle makers and the aftermarket.

name: Automotive Parts & Equipment
desc: Makers of parts, systems and electronics for vehicles.

name: Tires & Rubber
desc: Tire makers.

name: Automobiles
desc: Vehicle manufacturers.

name: Automobile Manufacturers
desc: Makers of passenger cars and light trucks, including electric vehicles.

name: Motorcycle Manufacturers
desc: Makers of motorcycles, scooters and three-wheelers.

name: Consumer Durables & Apparel
desc: Long-lasting goods for the home, leisure products, and clothing and footwear.

name: Household Durables
desc: Big-ticket goods for the home, and the homes themselves.

name: Consumer Electronics
desc: TVs, audio equipment, cameras and other consumer electronics.
note: Smartphones and PCs are in Information Technology (Technology Hardware, Storage & Peripherals).

name: Home Furnishings
desc: Furniture, mattresses, rugs and other furnishings.

name: Homebuilding
desc: Residential homebuilders and manufactured-home makers.

name: Household Appliances
desc: Washers, refrigerators, vacuums and other appliances, plus power tools and lawn equipment for home use.

name: Housewares & Specialties
desc: Cookware, tableware, storage and decorative products.

name: Leisure Products
desc: Things people buy for fun.

name: Leisure Products
desc: Toys, sporting goods, bicycles, recreational boats and similar products.

name: Textiles, Apparel & Luxury Goods
desc: What people wear.

name: Apparel, Accessories & Luxury Goods
desc: Clothing, handbags, jewelry and watches, including the luxury houses.

name: Footwear
desc: Makers of shoes and athletic footwear.

name: Textiles
desc: Producers of fabrics and textiles.

name: Consumer Services
desc: Experiences and services people pay for: travel, dining, gaming, education.

name: Hotels, Restaurants & Leisure
desc: Where people eat, stay and play.

name: Casinos & Gaming
desc: Casino operators, online betting companies and gaming equipment makers.

name: Hotels, Resorts & Cruise Lines
desc: Hotel and resort operators, cruise lines and online travel agencies.

name: Leisure Facilities
desc: Fitness clubs, theme parks, ski resorts and golf courses.

name: Restaurants
desc: Restaurant chains, fast food and coffee shops.

name: Diversified Consumer Services
desc: Services sold directly to individuals.

name: Education Services
desc: For-profit schools and universities, tutoring and online education.

name: Specialized Consumer Services
desc: Consumer services not covered elsewhere, such as funeral services and home services.

name: Consumer Discretionary Distribution & Retail
desc: Retailers and distributors of discretionary goods. Renamed from Retailing in the 2023 revision.

name: Distributors
desc: Wholesalers of consumer goods.

name: Distributors
desc: Wholesale distributors of discretionary consumer goods.

name: Broadline Retail
desc: Retailers that sell a bit of everything.

name: Broadline Retail
desc: Retailers offering a wide range of discretionary goods in stores or online, from department stores to online marketplaces.
note: Created in 2023 by merging Internet & Direct Marketing Retail with department and general merchandise stores. Amazon and Alibaba sit here.

name: Specialty Retail
desc: Retailers focused on one category.

name: Apparel Retail
desc: Clothing and accessories retailers.

name: Computer & Electronics Retail
desc: Consumer electronics and computer stores.

name: Home Improvement Retail
desc: Hardware and home improvement stores.

name: Other Specialty Retail
desc: Category retailers without their own sub-industry: books, sporting goods, jewelry, pet supplies, beauty.

name: Automotive Retail
desc: Car dealers, auto parts stores and gas station operators.

name: Homefurnishing Retail
desc: Furniture and home goods retailers.

name: Consumer Staples
desc: Necessities people buy regardless of the economy: food, drinks, household and personal products, and the stores that sell them.
drivers: Defensive demand that holds up in recessions
note: Since 2023, Walmart, Costco, Target and dollar stores sit here (Consumer Staples Merchandise Retail), moved from Consumer Discretionary.

name: Consumer Staples Distribution & Retail
desc: Grocers, pharmacies and big-box stores that mainly sell everyday necessities. Renamed from Food & Staples Retailing in 2023.

name: Consumer Staples Distribution & Retail
desc: The single industry in this group, covering four kinds of staples sellers.

name: Drug Retail
desc: Pharmacies and drugstore chains.

name: Food Distributors
desc: Wholesale distributors of food to restaurants, institutions and retailers.

name: Food Retail
desc: Supermarkets and grocery stores.

name: Consumer Staples Merchandise Retail
desc: Hypermarkets, warehouse clubs and discount stores that mainly sell staples.
note: New in 2023. Walmart, Costco, Target and dollar stores moved here.

name: Food, Beverage & Tobacco
desc: The makers of what people eat, drink and smoke.

name: Beverages
desc: Alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks.

name: Brewers
desc: Beer producers.

name: Distillers & Vintners
desc: Spirits and wine producers.

name: Soft Drinks & Non-alcoholic Beverages
desc: Soft drinks, bottled water, energy drinks and juices.

name: Food Products
desc: From farm commodities to branded packaged food.

name: Agricultural Products & Services
desc: Growers, processors and traders of crops, grains and livestock, and agricultural services.

name: Packaged Foods & Meats
desc: Branded and packaged foods, snacks, dairy, and meat and poultry processors.

name: Tobacco
desc: Cigarettes and other nicotine products.

name: Tobacco
desc: Makers of cigarettes and other tobacco and nicotine products.

name: Household & Personal Products
desc: Everyday products used around the home and on the body.

name: Household Products
desc: Products for keeping a home running.

name: Household Products
desc: Detergents, cleaners, paper towels, diapers and similar non-durable goods.

name: Personal Care Products
desc: Products people put on themselves. Renamed from Personal Products in 2023.

name: Personal Care Products
desc: Cosmetics, skin care, hair care, fragrance and toiletries.

name: Health Care
desc: Companies that deliver, pay for, equip and invent medical care.

name: Health Care Equipment & Services
desc: Physical products used in care, and the organizations that deliver and pay for it.

name: Health Care Equipment & Supplies
desc: Devices and consumables used by clinicians.

name: Health Care Equipment
desc: Medical devices, from surgical robots and imaging systems to implants and patient monitors.

name: Health Care Supplies
desc: Disposable medical supplies such as syringes, gloves, wound care and eye care consumables.

name: Health Care Providers & Services
desc: The businesses that deliver, distribute and pay for care.

name: Health Care Distributors
desc: Wholesale distributors of drugs and medical products to pharmacies and hospitals.

name: Health Care Services
desc: Diagnostic labs, outpatient and home health services, and pharmacy benefit managers.

name: Health Care Facilities
desc: Hospitals, nursing homes and rehabilitation centers.

name: Managed Health Care
desc: Health insurers and managed-care organizations.

name: Health Care Technology
desc: Software and IT for health care.

name: Health Care Technology
desc: Electronic health records, health IT services, telehealth and related software.

name: Pharmaceuticals, Biotechnology & Life Sciences
desc: Companies that discover, develop and make medicines, and the tools and services labs depend on.

name: Biotechnology
desc: Medicines from biology.

name: Biotechnology
desc: Companies developing therapies through genetic engineering and biological research. Many have no revenue yet and live on trial results.

name: Pharmaceuticals
desc: Drug makers.

name: Pharmaceuticals
desc: Branded and generic drug makers, including animal health.

name: Life Sciences Tools & Services
desc: Suppliers to the labs.

name: Life Sciences Tools & Services
desc: Lab instruments, reagents and consumables, and contract research and manufacturing for drug developers.

name: Financials
desc: Companies that lend, insure, move and manage money.
drivers: Interest rates and the shape of the yield curve
The credit cycle and loan losses
note: Visa, Mastercard and PayPal moved here from Information Technology in 2023. Equity REITs are a separate sector (Real Estate), but mortgage REITs stay in Financials.

name: Banks
desc: Deposit-taking lenders.

name: Banks
desc: Commercial banks, split by reach.

name: Diversified Banks
desc: Large banks with significant retail and commercial operations across regions or countries.

name: Regional Banks
desc: Banks focused on a region, lending mainly to small businesses and consumers.

name: Financial Services
desc: Financial firms that are neither banks nor insurers: payments, specialty lenders, asset managers, exchanges. Renamed from Diversified Financials in 2023.

name: Financial Services
desc: Payments, mortgage finance, holding companies and specialty finance.

name: Diversified Financial Services
desc: Firms offering a mix of financial services with no single dominant line.

name: Multi-Sector Holdings
desc: Holding companies with major stakes in unrelated industries.
note: Berkshire Hathaway is the best-known example.

name: Specialized Finance
desc: Niche financiers, such as specialty lenders and providers of financing for particular assets.

name: Commercial & Residential Mortgage Finance
desc: Mortgage lenders and servicers, including savings institutions focused on mortgages.
note: Absorbed the old Thrifts & Mortgage Finance industry in 2023.

name: Transaction & Payment Processing Services
desc: Card networks, payment processors and digital wallets.
note: New in 2023. Visa, Mastercard and PayPal moved here from Information Technology.

name: Consumer Finance
desc: Lending to individuals outside the banks.

name: Consumer Finance
desc: Credit card issuers, personal loans, auto loans and buy-now-pay-later lenders.

name: Capital Markets
desc: Firms that manage, trade and match capital.

name: Asset Management & Custody Banks
desc: Fund managers, private equity and alternatives firms, and custody banks.

name: Investment Banking & Brokerage
desc: Investment banks and retail and institutional brokers.

name: Diversified Capital Markets
desc: Firms with large, mixed capital-markets businesses.

name: Financial Exchanges & Data
desc: Stock and derivatives exchanges, and financial data and ratings providers.

name: Mortgage Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
desc: REITs that hold debt rather than buildings.

name: Mortgage REITs
desc: REITs that own mortgages and mortgage-backed securities instead of property.

name: Insurance
desc: Companies that take on risk for a premium, and those that broker it.

name: Insurance
desc: Five kinds of insurance business.

name: Insurance Brokers
desc: Intermediaries that place insurance for clients and earn commissions without taking underwriting risk.

name: Life & Health Insurance
desc: Life insurance, annuities and supplemental health coverage.

name: Multi-line Insurance
desc: Insurers with significant life and property-casualty businesses.

name: Property & Casualty Insurance
desc: Home, auto, commercial property and liability insurance.

name: Reinsurance
desc: Insurers that insure other insurers.

name: Information Technology
desc: Companies that make software, computers, networking gear and chips, and the services that run them.
note: Alphabet and Meta are not here; they moved to Communication Services in 2018. Payment companies left for Financials in 2023.

name: Software & Services
desc: Code, and the services built around it.

name: IT Services
desc: Help with building, running and hosting technology.

name: IT Consulting & Other Services
desc: IT consulting, systems integration and IT outsourcing.

name: Internet Services & Infrastructure
desc: Cloud and data-center services, web hosting, domain registration and content delivery networks.

name: Software
desc: Licensed and subscription software.

name: Application Software
desc: Software for business or consumer tasks: CRM, ERP, design, accounting, collaboration.

name: Systems Software
desc: Operating systems, databases, security and infrastructure software.

name: Technology Hardware & Equipment
desc: Physical technology: devices, networking gear and electronic components.

name: Communications Equipment
desc: Gear that carries data.

name: Communications Equipment
desc: Routers, switches, wireless and telecom equipment.

name: Technology Hardware, Storage & Peripherals
desc: Computers and devices.

name: Technology Hardware, Storage & Peripherals
desc: Smartphones, PCs, servers, storage devices and printers.

name: Electronic Equipment, Instruments & Components
desc: The parts inside, the instruments that test them, and the firms that assemble them.

name: Electronic Equipment & Instruments
desc: Test and measurement instruments and other electronic equipment.

name: Electronic Components
desc: Passive components, connectors, displays and sensors.

name: Electronic Manufacturing Services
desc: Contract manufacturers that assemble electronics for other brands.

name: Technology Distributors
desc: Distributors of technology products and components.

name: Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment
desc: Chips, and the machines and materials used to make them.

name: Semiconductors & Semiconductor Equipment
desc: The single industry in this group.

name: Semiconductor Materials & Equipment
desc: Makers of chipmaking tools and materials such as lithography systems, deposition equipment and wafers.

name: Semiconductors
desc: Chip designers and manufacturers, including foundries.
note: Solar cell and module makers are classified here too.

name: Communication Services
desc: Companies that connect people and capture their attention: telecom carriers, media, entertainment and online platforms.
note: Created in 2018 by widening the old Telecommunication Services sector to take in media companies from Consumer Discretionary and internet platforms from Information Technology.

name: Telecommunication Services
desc: Carriers that run voice and data networks.

name: Diversified Telecommunication Services
desc: Fixed-line and broadband carriers.

name: Alternative Carriers
desc: Newer or niche carriers such as fiber network operators and satellite communications.

name: Integrated Telecommunication Services
desc: Incumbent carriers offering fixed-line, broadband and often wireless service.

name: Wireless Telecommunication Services
desc: Mobile networks.

name: Wireless Telecommunication Services
desc: Mobile carriers whose business is mainly wireless.

name: Media & Entertainment
desc: Advertising, broadcasting, publishing, films, games and online platforms.

name: Media
desc: Traditional media and advertising.

name: Advertising
desc: Advertising agencies and marketing services.

name: Broadcasting
desc: Television and radio broadcasters.

name: Cable & Satellite
desc: Cable and satellite TV networks and operators.

name: Publishing
desc: Newspapers, magazines, books and digital publishing.

name: Entertainment
desc: Films, music, streaming and games.

name: Movies & Entertainment
desc: Film and TV studios, streaming services, music labels and live entertainment.

name: Interactive Home Entertainment
desc: Video game publishers and developers.

name: Interactive Media & Services
desc: Online platforms.

name: Interactive Media & Services
desc: Search engines, social networks and other online platforms that earn mainly from advertising.

name: Utilities
desc: Companies that generate and deliver electricity, gas and water.
drivers: Interest rates (the sector is capital-heavy and bond-like)
Electricity demand growth, including data centers

name: Utilities
desc: One industry group with five industries, split by what is delivered and whether it is regulated.

name: Electric Utilities
desc: Regulated electricity.

name: Electric Utilities
desc: Companies that generate, transmit and distribute electricity, mostly under regulation.

name: Gas Utilities
desc: Regulated gas.

name: Gas Utilities
desc: Companies that distribute natural gas to homes and businesses.

name: Multi-Utilities
desc: More than one service.

name: Multi-Utilities
desc: Utilities with significant operations in more than one of electricity, gas and water.

name: Water Utilities
desc: Water and wastewater.

name: Water Utilities
desc: Companies that supply water and treat wastewater.

name: Independent Power and Renewable Electricity Producers
desc: Generators that sell into markets rather than to captive customers.

name: Independent Power Producers & Energy Traders
desc: Unregulated generators selling power into wholesale markets, and energy traders.

name: Renewable Electricity
desc: Generators producing mainly from wind, solar, hydro and other renewables.

name: Real Estate
desc: Companies that own, develop and manage property, most of them structured as real estate investment trusts (REITs).
drivers: Supply pipelines in each property type
note: Split out of Financials in 2016 as the eleventh sector. Mortgage REITs stayed behind in Financials.

name: Equity Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
desc: REITs that own and operate property, grouped by the type of property they hold.

name: Diversified REITs
desc: Several property types.

name: Diversified REITs
desc: REITs that own a mix of property types with no single one dominant.

name: Industrial REITs
desc: Warehouses and logistics.

name: Industrial REITs
desc: Owners of warehouses, distribution centers and light industrial property.

name: Hotel & Resort REITs
desc: Lodging.

name: Hotel & Resort REITs
desc: Owners of hotels and resorts.

name: Office REITs
desc: Offices.

name: Office REITs
desc: Owners of office buildings.

name: Health Care REITs
desc: Medical property.

name: Health Care REITs
desc: Owners of senior housing, medical office buildings and hospitals.

name: Residential REITs
desc: Homes for rent.

name: Multi-Family Residential REITs
desc: Owners of apartment buildings.

name: Single-Family Residential REITs
desc: Owners of single-family rental homes and manufactured housing communities.

name: Retail REITs
desc: Shopping property.

name: Retail REITs
desc: Owners of malls, shopping centers and free-standing retail property.

name: Specialized REITs
desc: Property types with their own economics.

name: Other Specialized REITs
desc: Owners of specialized property without its own category, such as billboards, farmland and casinos.

name: Self-Storage REITs
desc: Owners of self-storage facilities.

name: Telecom Tower REITs
desc: Owners of cell towers and related wireless infrastructure.

name: Timber REITs
desc: Owners of timberland.

name: Data Center REITs
desc: Owners of data centers.

name: Real Estate Management & Development
desc: Real estate companies that are not REITs: developers, operators and service firms.

name: Real Estate Management & Development
desc: The single industry in this group.

name: Diversified Real Estate Activities
desc: Companies engaged in a mix of real estate activities.

name: Real Estate Operating Companies
desc: Companies that own and operate property but are not structured as REITs.

name: Real Estate Development
desc: Developers that build property to sell.

name: Real Estate Services
desc: Brokers, property managers, appraisers and other real estate service providers.
